rationale: bisort is a small, pointer- and recursion-heavy Olden benchmark whose hot path is recursive binary-tree sorting, so runtime overhead is the binding constraint while its simple, branch-light control flow limits the payoff of structural transformations. SUB and SPLIT are cheap, semantics-preserving, and safe, so they receive the highest weights across all dimensions to provide a baseline of instruction- and block-level resistance without meaningful cost. IBR gets a solid weight because hiding branch targets works well even in branch-light code and its overhead is acceptable, while ICALL and IGV are kept moderate since bisort has few call sites and globals to protect, capping their benefit. BCF and FLA are weighted lowest on the cost dimensions and only moderately on gain: both inflate code size and slow execution on hot recursive routines, and FLA in particular flattens little value out of bisort's shallow, structured control flow, so these passes should fire only on functions whose features strongly tolerate the overhead.
